items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1976-02-04
items.q: Bunk Johnson, Buddy Bowling, Freddie Keppard, Buddy Petit, and all these guys and he heard them

ctx.x: what was the difference in their style?

Well, there's a big difference. one was lyrical which from, from a classical vein, technically musical because Bix was a, uh, was interested in concert music and Debussy and Ravel and his thing was semi-classical, that In the Mist and a couple of piano pieces he wrote which had a, a great significance of creative inventiveness but based from a European, a classical vein where Louis stuff was so black out of the Baptist Church and out of the honky tonks and, uh, out of, uh, a tradition of New Orleans trumpet…

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I never heard Bunk at his heights, but I don’t think Bunk . . . My uncle Paul said Bunk was the greatest

ctx.x: Earlier. Before my time. Baquet was in that band. All them greats had been through that band. Papa Celestin. What’s his name? Bad man. Great trumpet player. His name phased out, because he was very unpopular, because he had a temper. King Oliver played in that band. Bunk Johnson played in that band. Before that Alcibiades Jeanjacque, he played in that band. He was a virtuoso trumpet player. Cornet player. Played in the circuses. He was supposed to go with Ringling Bros. in Ringling Bros.’s band, but they weren’t…

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Bunk Johnson booked a date for the longshoremen. And he forgot it!

ctx.x: Bunk Johnson booked a date for the longshoremen. And he forgot it! And the parade is waiting to go on, doin' with the umbrellas just like the Blacks. Same thing. And all of them rough Irish chicks is out there in the bar, and the band ain't comin'. And them sumbitches just... Heh...
